Your current working directory IS a git worktree of the podcast repo. Edit files there directly. Do NOT git commit/branch/push/stash. No MCP, no network, no model calls, no sending.

GRADING: a checker fails you for touching files outside the owned list, production change with no tests, fewer than 6 new def test_..., no negative test, or the verify command failing.

OWNED FILES (only these):
  server/pipeline/context_packet.py
  tests/test_context_packet_staleness.py
  tests/test_context_packet.py

WHAT THIS MODULE DOES. Before any outbound send, assemble_context_packet gathers live state (hubspot, gmail, calendar, funnel_state, send_holds) and emits a receipt. The gateway refuses to send when the receipt's verdict is "block". This is a genuinely valuable control and the fix must not weaken it.

THE DEFECT, measured on a real send today. A launch-announcement email to a podcast guest was blocked. The four blocking signals were:
    thread_recency_block: inbound message contains 'pushed'
    thread_recency_block: outbound message contains 'pushed'
    thread_recency_block: inbound message contains 'reschedule'
    thread_recency_block: inbound message contains 'reschedule'
Those words come from a June conversation about moving the recording date. The recording then HAPPENED on 22 July. The email being blocked was a 31 July announcement that the episode is live. A resolved scheduling discussion from five weeks earlier was blocking an unrelated announcement.

Reading _gmail_signals shows why: it scans subject/snippet/body of every returned message for BLOCK_KEYWORDS and emits a signal on any hit, with NO time decay, NO relation to what is being sent, and a name (thread_recency_block) that describes recency although the logic is a keyword match.

THE FIX — keep the control, remove the three defects:
1. TIME DECAY. A keyword hit only blocks when the message is recent. Add SIGNAL_RELEVANCE_DAYS (named constant, 21) with a comment citing this incident: a scheduling word from a conversation that has since been superseded by the event actually happening must not block. Messages older than that window produce an ADVISORY signal (recorded in the packet, does not set verdict=block) rather than a blocking one. Parse the message date defensively; a message whose date cannot be parsed is treated as RECENT (fail-closed), never as old.
2. ACTION RELEVANCE. Scheduling keywords (postpone, reschedule, pushed, push back, move it, move this, move our) are relevant to a send that is itself about scheduling, and not to an announcement. Add a mapping from action kind to the keyword groups that can block it. Group the existing BLOCK_KEYWORDS into at least SCHEDULING and CONSENT/STOP groups; consent-or-stop style keywords (anything indicating the person wants no contact, wants something removed, or is unhappy) block EVERY action kind and must never be filtered out by relevance. Default for an unknown action kind is to apply ALL groups, so a new kind is fail-closed rather than unfiltered.
3. NAMING. Rename the emitted signal kind from thread_recency_block to something that describes what it is, e.g. gmail_keyword_block, and keep the old string accepted anywhere the codebase matches on it so nothing breaks. Note the rename in a comment.

Do NOT change: the source list, the send_holds source, the CRM status blocking, the receipt schema, or the gateway's refusal behaviour on verdict=block.

TESTS (tests/test_context_packet_staleness.py; at least 6). Use the REAL incident as the primary fixture:
 (1) THE INCIDENT: a gmail source whose only keyword hits are 'pushed'/'reschedule' in messages dated 40 days before `now`, for action kind "guest_promo_email", yields a receipt whose verdict is NOT block, and the stale hits appear as advisory;
 (2) NEGATIVE: the same keywords in a message dated 2 days before `now` DO block — recency still bites;
 (3) NEGATIVE: a consent/stop keyword blocks regardless of age AND regardless of action kind — assert with an old message and an unrelated kind, proving relevance filtering can never suppress it;
 (4) NEGATIVE: a message with an unparseable date is treated as recent and blocks — fail-closed;
 (5) an unknown action kind applies all keyword groups (fail-closed default);
 (6) scheduling keywords still block a scheduling-type action even when the announcement type would ignore them;
 (7) the emitted signal kind is the new name, and any existing consumer matching the old name still functions.
